sections.overview: The Alpine pika is a small, plant-eating lagomorph of the Altai and Sayan mountain region of Central and East Asia.
sections.identification: It is a compact, short-eared mammal with a brown summer coat that becomes greyer in winter. Distinguishing it from other *Ochotona* may require careful taxonomic work, since related pikas occur across the region.
sections.habitat: It occupies rocky slopes and talus with nearby vegetation, across mountain ranges in Russia, Mongolia, Kazakhstan and northern China. Patches of suitable rock habitat are naturally fragmented.
sections.diet: It is a generalist herbivore. Pikas gather and store plants in haypiles for winter, when snow limits access to fresh forage.
sections.behavior: It is mainly active by day and gives sharp calls. Haypiles can also provide winter food for other herbivores when snow is deep.
sections.reproduction: A species account reports two litters a year, averaging about three young per litter, but reproductive data are limited and should not be generalized to every population.
sections.ecology: Its feeding and haypiles can influence local vegetation and provide food for other animals. These interactions are reported for particular sites, rather than measured across the whole range.
sections.conservation: The IUCN assessment published in 2016 classified it as Least Concern and described the trend as stable, while noting sparse population information and possible fluctuations in isolated populations.
